terms.short: Right, not obligation, to buy or sell
terms.definition: A contract giving the buyer the right, but not the obligation, to buy or sell an asset at a set price on or before a set date. The seller takes on the obligation in return for the premium.
examples: We'd rather buy options than futures into the event, so our loss is capped at the premium.
terms.fill: Unlike a future, an ____ gives the buyer a right but not an obligation to trade.
wrong: Obligation to buy or sell at a set price on a set date
Share that pays a fixed dividend
Loan that can be repaid early

tf.s: The buyer of an option can lose more than the premium paid.

terms.short: Right to buy at the strike
terms.definition: An option that gives the buyer the right to buy the underlying at the strike price. It gains value as the underlying rises.
examples: We bought Nifty calls ahead of the RBI policy.
terms.fill: If you expect Reliance to rally but want limited risk, you could buy a ____.
wrong: Right to sell at the strike
Obligation to buy at the strike
Request from the broker for more margin

tf.s: A call option gains value when the underlying falls.

calcs.q: You buy a 24,000 call for 150. At expiry Nifty is at 24,400. Profit per unit?
calcs.why: Intrinsic value 400 minus the 150 premium paid = 250.

terms.short: Right to sell at the strike
terms.definition: An option that gives the buyer the right to sell the underlying at the strike price. It gains value as the underlying falls.
examples: We bought index puts to protect the portfolio into the election results.
terms.fill: To protect a stock you own against a crash, you can buy a ____ on it.
wrong: Right to buy at the strike
Obligation to sell at the market price
Order to sell at the best available price

calcs.q: You buy a 1,000 put for 30. At expiry the stock is at 940. Profit per share?

terms.short: Price the option lets you trade at
terms.definition: The fixed price at which the option holder can buy (for a call) or sell (for a put) the underlying.
examples: The 24,000 strike has the most open interest this week.
terms.fill: A 1,500 call lets you buy the stock at 1,500, which is its ____.
wrong: Price you pay to buy the option
Current market price of the stock
Price at which the option last traded

terms.definition: The price the buyer pays the seller for an option. It equals intrinsic value plus time value.
examples: Premiums are rich ahead of the budget because implied vol is high.
terms.fill: An option buyer's maximum loss is the ____ paid.
wrong: Strike price of the option
Margin the option seller posts
Profit made at expiry

terms.short: Asset a derivative is based on
terms.definition: The asset whose price a derivative tracks, such as a stock, an index like the Nifty 50, a currency or a commodity.
examples: The underlying moved 2% but the option moved 30%.
terms.fill: For a Bank Nifty option, the ____ is the Bank Nifty index.
wrong: Strike price of a derivative
Broker who executes the trade
Lowest price of the day

terms.definition: The date on which an option or future ends. At expiry an option either settles for its intrinsic value or expires worthless.
examples: Most of the open interest sits in the nearest weekly contract, so expiry day this week will be lively.
terms.fill: On the day of ____, out-of-the-money options become worthless.
wrong: Date the option was first listed
Last day to pay the premium
Date dividends are paid
terms.note: Indian options are European style: they can only be exercised at expiry. Index options settle in cash; stock options settle by delivery of shares.

terms.definition: An option that would be worth exercising now: a call with its strike below the underlying price, or a put with its strike above it.
examples: The 23,500 call is 500 points in the money.
terms.fill: With Nifty at 24,000, a 23,800 call is ____.
wrong: Call with its strike above the underlying price
Option that has made a profit for its buyer
Option trading above its theoretical value

calcs.q: Nifty is at 24,000. Which of these options is in the money?
calcs.why: A put is in the money when its strike is above the underlying: 24,200 is above 24,000.

terms.definition: An option with no intrinsic value: a call with its strike above the underlying price, or a put with its strike below it. Its whole premium is time value.
examples: Retail traders love buying far out-of-the-money calls on expiry day.
terms.fill: With Nifty at 24,000, a 24,500 call is ____, so its premium is pure time value.
wrong: Call with its strike below the underlying price
Option that has lost money for its buyer
Option that can no longer be traded

terms.short: Strike at or near the current price
terms.definition: An option whose strike is at, or closest to, the current price of the underlying. ATM options carry the most time value and, near expiry, the most gamma.
examples: Sell the ATM straddle and you collect the most premium, and take the most risk.
terms.fill: With Nifty at 24,010, the 24,000 strike is the option that is ____.
wrong: Strike far below the current price
Option sitting exactly at its break-even
Option trading at the same price as yesterday

terms.definition: What an option would be worth if exercised now: underlying minus strike for a call, strike minus underlying for a put, and never below zero.
examples: The call trades at 260 and has 200 of intrinsic value.
terms.fill: A 23,800 call with Nifty at 24,000 has 200 points of ____.
wrong: Value that comes from the time left to expiry
Fair value from the Black-Scholes model
Total premium of the option
terms.formula: call: max(S − K, 0) · put: max(K − S, 0)

calcs.q: A stock is at 1,250. What is the intrinsic value of the 1,200 call?
A stock is at 1,250. What is the intrinsic value of the 1,200 put?
calcs.why: Strike 1,200 − price 1,250 is negative, and intrinsic value never goes below zero.

terms.definition: The part of an option's premium above its intrinsic value. It reflects the time left and expected volatility, and shrinks to zero at expiry.
examples: Most of what you pay for a weekly OTM option is time value, and it melts fast.
terms.fill: An out-of-the-money option's premium is made up entirely of ____.
wrong: Value if exercised right now
Number of days left to expiry
Interest earned on margin

calcs.q: A call trades at 260 and has 200 of intrinsic value. What is its time value?

terms.definition: Measures, named mostly after Greek letters, of how an option's price changes when one input moves: the underlying (delta, gamma), time (theta), volatility (vega) and interest rates (rho).
examples: Before adding size, check the book's Greeks, not just its P&L.
terms.fill: Traders run an options book by watching delta, gamma, theta and vega, together called the ____.
wrong: Options listed on the Athens exchange
Ratios used to value a company
Strikes with the most open interest

terms.definition: How much an option's price changes for a 1-point move in the underlying. Call deltas run from 0 to 1, put deltas from 0 to −1, and an at-the-money option sits near 0.5.
examples: We're long 0.3-delta calls, so a 100-point rally makes us about 30 points on each.
terms.fill: A call with a ____ of 0.6 gains about 60 paise when the stock rises ₹1.
wrong: Change in option price as one day passes
Change in option price per 1-point move in volatility
Change in delta per 1-point move in the underlying
terms.note: Delta is also read as a rough probability of ending in the money, and as a share equivalent: 10 calls of 0.5 delta behave like 5 units of the underlying.

tf.s: A put option has a negative delta.

calcs.q: A call has delta 0.6. Nifty rises 50 points. Roughly how much does the call gain?
You hold 10 lots of calls with delta 0.4. That's like holding how many lots of the underlying?

terms.definition: How much an option's delta changes for a 1-point move in the underlying. Gamma is highest for at-the-money options close to expiry, which is why their deltas swing so fast.
examples: Expiry-day gamma on the ATM strike makes the hedges jumpy.
terms.fill: Close to expiry, at-the-money options have very high ____, so their delta can flip from 0.2 to 0.8 in one move.
wrong: Change in option price per 1-point move in the underlying
Change in option price as one day passes
Change in option price per 1-point move in implied volatility

tf.s: Buying options gives you positive gamma.

calcs.q: A call has delta 0.50 and gamma 0.002 per point. The underlying rises 100 points. New delta is about?

terms.short: Value lost as each day passes
terms.definition: How much an option's price changes as one day passes, all else equal. Long options usually have negative theta: they lose a little value every day.
examples: We're short options, so theta pays us about ₹2 lakh a day if nothing moves.
terms.fill: An option buyer who is right on direction but too slow can still lose money to ____.
wrong: Change in option price per 1-point move in the underlying
Change in option price per 1-point move in volatility
Change in option price per 1% move in interest rates

tf.s: Option sellers usually benefit as theta erodes the premium.

calcs.q: An option has theta of −8 points a day. If nothing else changes, how much does it lose over 3 days?

terms.short: Change per 1-point move in implied vol
terms.definition: How much an option's price changes when implied volatility moves by 1 percentage point. Long options have positive vega.
examples: We're long vega into the results, so we want IV to rise.
terms.fill: If implied volatility drops 3 points, an option with a ____ of 12 loses about 36.
wrong: Change in option price as one day passes
Change in delta per 1-point move in the underlying
Change in option price per 1% move in interest rates
terms.note: Vega is not actually a Greek letter; the name stuck anyway.

calcs.q: An option has vega of 12. Implied vol falls from 18% to 15%. The option changes by about?

terms.short: Change per 1% move in interest rates
terms.definition: How much an option's price changes when interest rates move by 1 percentage point. Calls have positive rho and puts negative. It matters most for long-dated options.
examples: Rho barely matters on weekly options, but on a two-year option it adds up.
terms.fill: For short-dated index options, ____ is the Greek traders watch least, since rate changes barely move the price.
wrong: Change in option price per 1-point move in volatility
Change in delta as one day passes
Change in option price per 1-point move in the underlying

terms.definition: The volatility of the underlying that, fed into a pricing model, gives the option's market price. It shows how big a move the market is pricing in.
examples: IV on Bank Nifty jumped to 18 ahead of the policy.
terms.fill: When options get expensive before an event, traders say ____ has gone up.
wrong: How much the price actually moved last month
Average daily range of the stock
Volatility limit set by the exchange

terms.definition: Buying or selling the underlying or its futures so that a position's total delta is close to zero, removing exposure to small price moves.
examples: We sold calls and hedged the delta with Nifty futures.
terms.fill: After selling calls worth 40 deltas, the trader bought 40 units of futures, a textbook case of ____.
wrong: Buying more options as they fall
Selling options to collect time decay
Closing all positions before expiry

calcs.q: You are short 100 calls with delta 0.4 each. To be delta neutral you should…
calcs.why: Short 100 × 0.4 = −40 delta, so buying 40 units brings it to zero.

terms.definition: A position whose total delta is about zero, so small moves in the underlying barely change its value. Its P&L then comes from gamma, theta and vega.
examples: The book is delta neutral; we're really trading volatility.
terms.fill: A straddle starts out roughly ____, because the call's positive delta offsets the put's negative delta.
wrong: Position with no options in it
Position that cannot lose money
Position whose gamma is zero

tf.s: A delta-neutral position cannot lose money.

terms.short: Hurt by big moves either way
terms.definition: A position, usually from selling options, that loses on big moves in either direction and must hedge by buying high and selling low. Long gamma is the opposite and gains from big moves.
examples: Dealers were short gamma into expiry, so every move got amplified.
terms.fill: Option sellers are ____: large moves in either direction hurt them.
wrong: Holding only a small options position
Having a negative delta
Owning options that expire soon

tf.s: Being short gamma usually comes with positive theta.

terms.definition: The standard model for pricing European options from five inputs: underlying price, strike, time to expiry, interest rate and volatility. Most Greeks shown on trading screens come from it.
examples: Our IV numbers come from Black-Scholes, adjusted for dividends.
terms.fill: Feed the market price into the ____ and solve for volatility, and you get implied vol.
wrong: Rule for splitting profits between partners
Model for valuing a company's shares from dividends
Index of option prices on NSE

tf.s: Black-Scholes assumes volatility stays constant over the option's life.

terms.short: How much the price actually moved
terms.definition: The volatility the underlying actually showed over a past period, usually measured as the annualised standard deviation of daily returns.
examples: IV is 16 but realised is only 11, so options look rich.
terms.fill: If implied vol sits far above ____, options look expensive compared with how much the market has really moved.
wrong: Volatility implied by option prices
Exchange's estimate of next month's moves
Volatility of the bid-ask spread

terms.definition: The pattern of implied volatility across strikes for one expiry. On equity indices, out-of-the-money puts usually carry higher IV than calls, because investors pay up for crash protection.
examples: Put skew steepened as everyone bought downside before the budget.
terms.fill: Downside Nifty puts trade at a higher implied vol than upside calls; traders call this the ____.
wrong: Implied vol differing across expiry dates
Gap between implied and realised vol
Lopsidedness of a return distribution

terms.short: Implied vol higher at both wings
terms.definition: A pattern where both far out-of-the-money puts and calls carry higher implied volatility than at-the-money options, so the curve looks like a smile. Common in currencies and around big events.
examples: Ahead of the election result, the curve turned into a smile: both wings got bid.
terms.fill: If far puts and far calls both trade at higher IV than the ATM strike, the curve forms a ____.
wrong: Implied vol rising steadily with expiry
Implied vol falling after an event
Pattern of open interest across strikes

terms.definition: How implied volatility varies across expiry dates. It usually slopes upward in calm markets and inverts, with near expiries higher, in stress or before known events.
examples: Weekly IV is above monthly ahead of the budget, so the curve is inverted.
terms.fill: Near-dated IV is above longer-dated IV ahead of the budget, so the ____ is inverted.
wrong: Implied vol across strikes for one expiry
Interest rates across maturities
Realised vol across past years

terms.short: Sharp fall in IV after an event
terms.definition: A sudden drop in implied volatility once a known event such as results or a policy decision has passed. Option buyers can lose money even when the stock moves their way.
examples: We were right on direction, but IV crush after results ate the gain.
terms.fill: After the RBI decision, implied vol collapsed from 20 to 12, a classic ____.
wrong: Sharp rise in implied vol before an event
Fall in open interest at expiry
Forced selling by option buyers

tf.s: An option buyer can lose money after results even if the stock moves the way they expected.

terms.definition: NSE's volatility index, calculated from Nifty 50 option prices. It shows the market's expected annualised volatility over the next 30 days.
examples: The VIX spiked above 20 into the election results.
terms.fill: Traders call ____ the fear gauge of the Indian market.
wrong: Index of the most traded Nifty options
NSE's measure of last month's actual price swings
Index of the 20 most volatile stocks

calcs.q: India VIX is at 16. Roughly what daily Nifty move does that imply?

terms.short: Fixed link between call, put and forward
terms.definition: The no-arbitrage link between a European call and put with the same strike and expiry: call minus put equals the underlying price minus the present value of the strike.
examples: The puts look cheap against the calls; put-call parity says someone will arb that.
terms.fill: If calls get too expensive against puts of the same strike, arbitrageurs restore ____.
wrong: Rule that calls and puts always cost the same
Ratio of put to call open interest
Rule that a call and a put cancel each other out

calcs.q: Ignoring interest rates, a 100-strike call costs 8 and the stock is at 105. What should the 100-strike put cost?

terms.short: How far in or out of the money
terms.definition: Where an option's strike sits relative to the underlying price, in, at or out of the money, often measured as strike divided by spot or by delta.
examples: Compare skew by moneyness, say 25-delta puts against 25-delta calls.
terms.fill: To compare options across strikes, traders describe their ____, such as 95% of spot or 25 delta.
wrong: How much money an option position has made
Cash needed to buy one lot
Premium per point of the underlying

terms.definition: The number of futures or option contracts outstanding that have not yet been closed or settled. Rising open interest with rising prices suggests fresh long positions.
examples: The highest call OI sits at 24,500, so traders treat it as resistance.
terms.fill: Volume counts contracts traded today; ____ counts contracts still open at the end of the day.
wrong: Number of contracts traded today
Interest charged on margin loans
Number of traders holding the option

terms.short: Put open interest ÷ call open interest
terms.definition: Open interest (or volume) in puts divided by that in calls. A high ratio shows heavy put buying or writing; traders read it in different ways and often as a contrarian signal.
examples: PCR is above 1.3, so a lot of put writing is supporting the market.
terms.fill: Put open interest divided by call open interest gives the ____.
wrong: Price of a put divided by price of a call
Ratio of option volume to futures volume
Number of puts per lot

calcs.q: Put OI is 1.2 crore contracts and call OI is 1.0 crore. The PCR is?

terms.definition: How much an option's delta changes when implied volatility moves, which equals how much vega changes when the underlying moves. It matters for skew trades and for dealers hedging large out-of-the-money positions.
examples: As vol collapsed after the event, vanna pulled the delta of those OTM puts toward zero and dealers bought back their hedges.
terms.fill: If a fall in implied vol changes your delta even though spot hasn't moved, you're seeing ____ at work.
wrong: Change in vega for a move in volatility
Change in delta as time passes
Change in gamma for a move in the underlying

tf.s: Vanna links changes in volatility to changes in delta.

terms.definition: How much an option's vega changes when implied volatility moves: the convexity of an option's value in volatility. Out-of-the-money options carry the most of it.
examples: We own the wings for the vomma: if vol spikes, our vega grows with it.
terms.fill: A trader long far out-of-the-money options picks up more vega as vol rises, thanks to positive ____.
wrong: Change in delta for a move in volatility
Change in gamma as time passes
Change in vega as time passes

terms.definition: How much an option's delta changes as one day passes, all else equal. Over a weekend or close to expiry it can shift hedges noticeably.
examples: Monday's hedge was off because charm shrank our OTM deltas over the weekend.
terms.fill: Even with the market flat, out-of-the-money deltas shrink each day because of ____.
wrong: Change in vega as time passes
Change in gamma as time passes
Change in option price as time passes

terms.short: Gamma's change per move in spot
terms.definition: How much gamma changes for a 1-point move in the underlying: a third-order Greek showing how quickly gamma itself shifts as the price moves.
examples: Speed tells us how fast our gamma explodes if spot runs toward the strike.
terms.fill: To know how fast gamma will grow as spot runs toward the strike, look at ____.
wrong: Change in gamma as time passes
Change in gamma for a move in volatility
Change in delta per 1-point move in spot

terms.definition: How much an option's gamma changes as one day passes. For at-the-money options gamma rises sharply into expiry, and this Greek measures that drift.
examples: The ATM gamma on our book will double by Thursday; color says how fast.
terms.fill: Gamma on at-the-money strikes rises each day into expiry, a drift measured by ____.
wrong: Change in delta as time passes
Change in gamma for a move in spot
Change in vega as time passes

terms.definition: How much gamma changes when implied volatility moves. Lower volatility concentrates gamma near the strike; higher volatility spreads it out across strikes.
examples: Vol fell and our ATM gamma jumped: that's zomma.
terms.fill: If vol falls and the gamma of your at-the-money options jumps, that's ____.
wrong: Change in delta for a move in volatility
Change in gamma for a move in spot
Change in vega for a move in volatility

terms.definition: How much an option's vega changes as one day passes. Vega shrinks as expiry approaches, so a vol position gets smaller on its own.
examples: Our vega halves by expiry week; veta is why the vol bet fades.
terms.fill: A long-vol position gets smaller each day even if nothing moves, because of ____.
wrong: Change in vega for a move in volatility
Change in delta as time passes
Change in option price per 1-point move in volatility

terms.definition: A third-order Greek: how much vomma changes when implied volatility moves. It matters mainly to desks running large volatility books.
examples: In a vol spike, ultima tells the desk how fast its vomma will change.
terms.fill: The third-order Greek that tracks how vomma changes with volatility is ____.
wrong: Change in gamma for a move in spot
Change in vega as time passes
Change in delta for a move in volatility

terms.definition: The percentage change in an option's price for a 1% move in the underlying. It shows how much leverage the option carries.
examples: Far OTM calls have huge lambda, which is why they feel like lottery tickets.
terms.fill: With a ____ of 10, a 1% rise in the stock lifts the call about 10%.
wrong: Points the option moves per 1-point move in the underlying
Change in delta per 1% move
Option price as a percentage of the strike

calcs.q: Stock at 100, call price 5, delta 0.5. What is the call's lambda?
calcs.why: 0.5 × 100 ÷ 5 = 10, so a 1% stock move moves the call about 10%.

terms.short: Own the stock, sell a call on it
terms.definition: Holding a stock and selling a call option on it to earn premium, giving up any gain above the strike.
examples: The fund runs covered calls on its banks to squeeze extra income in a flat market.
terms.fill: A fund that owns HDFC Bank and sells monthly calls on it for income is running a ____.
wrong: Owning a stock and buying a put on it
Buying a call and selling a higher-strike call
Selling a call without owning the stock

terms.short: Own the stock, buy a put on it
terms.definition: Buying a put on a stock or index you own, so losses below the strike are capped. It works like insurance.
examples: We bought protection with 5% OTM puts for the quarter.
terms.fill: Before the election, the PM bought a ____ on the Nifty to cap the portfolio's downside.
wrong: Owning a stock and selling a call on it
Selling a put to collect premium
Buying a call and a put at the same strike

terms.short: Call and put at the same strike
terms.definition: Buying (or selling) a call and a put with the same strike and expiry. A long straddle profits from a big move either way; a short straddle profits if the market stays still.
examples: The ATM straddle is pricing a 3% move on results day.
terms.fill: Expecting a big move after results but unsure of the direction, she bought a ____.
wrong: Call and put at different out-of-the-money strikes
Buying a call and selling a higher call
Same strike, different expiries

calcs.q: You buy the 24,000 straddle for 400 in total. Where are the break-evens at expiry?

terms.short: OTM call and OTM put together
terms.definition: Buying (or selling) an out-of-the-money call and an out-of-the-money put with the same expiry. Cheaper than a straddle, but it needs a bigger move to pay off.
examples: We sold the 23,500–24,500 strangle and collected 120.
terms.fill: Buying a 24,500 call and a 23,500 put on the same expiry is a ____.
wrong: Call and put at the same strike
Buying a put and selling a lower put
Owning stock and selling a call

terms.short: Buy a call, sell a higher call
terms.definition: Buying a call and selling a higher-strike call on the same expiry. It costs less than a call alone but caps the profit at the higher strike.
examples: Calls were pricey, so we did the 24,000–24,500 call spread instead.
terms.fill: To cut the cost of a bullish bet, he bought the 24,000 call and sold the 24,500 call: a ____.
wrong: Buying a call and a put at one strike
Selling a near call and buying a far one at the same strike
Owning stock and selling a call

calcs.q: Buy the 100 call for 6 and sell the 110 call for 2. Maximum profit at expiry?

terms.definition: Selling an out-of-the-money put spread and an out-of-the-money call spread together. It earns premium if the market stays in a range, and the bought wings cap the loss.
examples: We run weekly iron condors when VIX is high and the range is clear.
terms.fill: To earn premium in a range-bound market while capping losses with bought wings, traders sell an ____.
wrong: Buying a straddle with extra calls
Buying calls at three strikes
Selling a near option and buying a far one

terms.definition: Selling a near-expiry option and buying a longer-dated option at the same strike. It profits from faster decay in the near option and from a rise in longer-dated implied vol.
examples: Weekly IV is rich, so sell the weekly and buy the monthly in a calendar.
terms.fill: Selling this week's 24,000 call and buying next month's 24,000 call is a ____.
wrong: Same expiry, different strikes
Call and put at the same strike
Rolling a futures position to the next month

terms.short: Trading the hedge on a long-gamma book
terms.definition: Holding long options and repeatedly re-hedging delta: selling the underlying as it rises and buying as it falls. It makes money if realised volatility beats the implied volatility paid.
examples: We're long the straddle and gamma scalping the futures around it.
terms.fill: A trader long a straddle who sells futures on rallies and buys on dips to stay hedged is ____.
wrong: Selling options and hoping nothing moves
Buying options just before expiry
Taking small intraday profits in the cash market

tf.s: Gamma scalping makes money when realised volatility is higher than the implied volatility paid.

terms.short: Price sits on a strike at expiry
terms.definition: The risk that the underlying closes right at a strike on expiry, leaving an option seller unsure whether the option will be exercised and what position they will end up holding.
examples: The stock closed a rupee from our short strike; pin risk means we don't know our delivery position until tonight.
terms.fill: When the stock closes right at the strike on expiry, the option seller faces ____.
wrong: Risk that an exchange halts trading
Risk of a fat-finger order
Risk that the option is mispriced at listing
